She let go. They both paused.
“Come,” he invited at last. He gestured her toward the table and settled down onto a chair with the ease of someone who has spent a good deal of time sitting in it.
Mara took the nearest empty seat, pulled it up to the table, sat down. The edge of a green leather cushion pressed into her thighs, and she crossed one leg over the other.
Jonah was looking at her again.
“You’re early,” he observed.
She cleared her throat. “I took your advice. I saw the place at daylight.”
He nodded. “I do it all the time. You should too.”
She raised an eyebrow. “Do what?”
His eyes danced. “Stay here, if you like it. You can use my lab. And you’ll get used to Livia. She’s not as scary as she looks.”
“Is that so.” Mara tilted her head, keeping her voice level. “And how exactly would I accomplish the ‘staying,’ in the absence of an offer to stay?”
text:
When Mara walked into the common room at six fifteen, someone was already there. Someone younger, it seemed.
She couldn’t make out the face behind the blond hair. But the body was fine enough, leaning back on the couch with bare legs crossed and arms flung in opposite directions, one palm pressing the padded wall and the other wrist resting on the low table beside him.
She stood stock-still by the doorway for a moment, aware of her breath and of his awareness that she was here. He stirred and tilted his head; a face turned toward her, expressionless.

The two pairs of eyes held each other through an entire exhale.
And then the young man had pushed himself up on the armrests, stretched to his full height, and strolled over to shake her hand.
“Mara?”
He was closer than she would have guessed from where he’d been sitting, broad-shouldered and strong-chinned in a white T-shirt, grinning at her through dark-framed glasses as he reached out for the handshake. She took it.
“Jonah,” he said.
“Hello,” she replied, and then they stood there, still shaking hands, not knowing what to do next.

segment:
Jonah looked down at their locked hands, and then back at Mara, and then he pulled them apart—but just a little—and turned his free hand so he could link fingers with her again in an arm-in-arm gesture.
He’d put his arms around her waist, she realized after a moment, and she leaned forward to meet him. It felt like the first time she’d ever touched another person that way—and it didn’t seem to be going too badly, though she couldn’t really tell if she was doing it right or not.

After a while he pulled back enough to let go of her, then took another step toward her.
